therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: BRAF kinase inhibition combined with MEK inhibition and optional CDK4/6 inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Dual blockade of MAPK pathway to overcome resistance and enhance tumor cell growth inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adult patients with BRAF V600 mutation-positive advanced solid tumors
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Phase 1b: Dose limiting toxicities; Phase 2: Disease control rate at week 16 (mCRC), Objective response rate (melanoma arms)

results.effect_size: Phase 2 ORR: mCRC 63.6% (95% CI: 30.8-89.1), Prior BRAFi Melanoma 42.3% (95% CI: 23.4-63.1), BRAFi-naïve Melanoma 66.7% (95% CI: 50.5-80.4), Triple combination 59.5% (95% CI: 43.3-74.4)
results.target_engagement_evidence: Extensive PK data showing dose-proportional exposure for encorafenib, binimetinib, and ribociclib with appropriate steady-state levels achieved
biomarker_changes: BRAF V600 mutations confirmed in majority of patients
Some patients had additional alterations in PTEN, PIK3CA, MAP2K1
subgroup_findings: BRAFi-naïve melanoma patients had higher response rates than BRAFi-pretreated patients
Triple combination did not show clear superiority over dual combination
safety_signals: Retinal toxicity (retinal detachment, retinal vein occlusion)
Grade 3/4 AEs common across dose levels
results.dose_information: Phase 1b dose escalation from 50-800mg encorafenib + 45mg binimetinib +/- 100-600mg ribociclib; Phase 2 used established doses

context.comparator: No control arm - single arm study
context.duration: Maximum treatment exposure 118.3 months (Phase 1b) and 111.5 months (Phase 2)
